scope.description: Eligibility of response support consumed by VerifyLeader in an established leader tenure and unchanged configuration. Distinguish eligible voter acknowledgement from successful communication with a nonvoter.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine peers, intact current configuration and no concurrent configuration change.
The leader is an eligible voter; response observations refer to the same verification operation.
excluded: Global linearizable-read endpoint or election-safety violation
Bounded eventual completion in the absence of a voter quorum

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: No target source changes. skipStartup suppresses autonomous timers and goroutines; the driver runs peer RPC consumers.
Campaign-loop scheduling is replaced by consuming real electSelf vote responses and applying the sourced majority transition; configuration remains the bootstrapped fixed configuration.

The driver materializes per-peer worker structs from startStopReplication initialization and schedules only the selected heartbeat after verifyLeader registers the future. Other worker replies are delayed beyond this observation interval.
No runLeader no-op or FSM application is required for the selected verifyLeader entry; the check stops at tally/threshold notification rather than claiming public API completion.
Transport wrapper stops its heartbeat after the actual underlying RPC returns, independently of tally outcome. Timers are long to leave the bounded schedule before lease/election expiry.

plan_uncertainties: The check observes tally and threshold notification, not VerifyLeader Future success or a client read endpoint.
Campaign scheduling and worker creation are explicit driver substitutions; actual election grants and actual selected heartbeat receiver execute in the same per-case history.

boundaries: Global linearizable-read endpoint or election-safety violation
Bounded eventual completion in the absence of a voter quorum
